# OmniPhysicsVolumeDeformableSimAPI

Marks the tetrahedral simulation mesh of a volume deformable body and carries its rest shape. The walker accepts it on the body [prim](glossary.md#prim) or an immediate child that is a TetMesh or has readable tetVertexIndices; volume cooking requires the rest shape to match the mesh exactly.

- **Applies to:** `TetMesh`
- **Read only when listed in [`usd-schemas`](prim.md#columns).**
- **No builder:** `ovphysx.population` and `Population.hpp` do not write this component; the consumer reads it when another population writes it.

## Columns

*Raw fallback* is the [USD](glossary.md#usd) schema value. *Producer writes* is what [ovstage](glossary.md#ovstage) population puts in the column for a USD stage. *Parser default* applies on the consumer when the column is absent, in stage units. **diverges** means writing the raw fallback literally parses differently from omitting the column (the parser default): USD population may well publish that very value for an unauthored attribute, so the marker is about the column being present, not about its value.

| Column | Type | Units | Raw fallback | Producer writes | Parser default | If absent |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `omniphysics:restShapePoints` | float32[3] array, POINT | length |  | not written |  | Volume cooking requires exactly one rest point per simulation-mesh point, so an absent column fails cooking ('UsdGeomTetMesh not compatible with rest attributes in DeformableVolumeSimAPI') and no body is created. For a PhysxAutoDeformableBodyAPI body the runtime's cooker generates the simulation mesh and writes this column itself. |
| `omniphysics:restTetVtxIndices` | int32[4] array | none |  | not written |  | Volume cooking requires it to equal tetVertexIndices element for element, so an absent column fails cooking with the same error and no body is created. Written by the cooker for a PhysxAutoDeformableBodyAPI body. |

## Notes

- ovstage's [usd-prim-type](prim.md#columns) column reports a UsdGeomTetMesh as [Mesh](glossary.md#mesh), so the walker also accepts a prim with readable tetVertexIndices.
